alignment.note: Greek uses article + postpositive δέ (ὁ δέ, 'but he') and Syriac mirrors this with ܗܘ ܕܝܢ; the Vulgate compresses subject and adversative into the relative pronoun Qui, dropping any explicit rendering of δέ and shifting from paratactic to relative-clause construction.

Greek ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ and Vulgate in verbo render 'at the word'; the Peshitta adds the demonstrative ܗܕܐ ('this'), specifying ܒܡܠܬܐ ܗܕܐ ('at this word/saying'), a typical Syriac clarifying expansion absent from the Greek and Latin.

Greek λυπούμενος and Vulgate mœrens render the participle 'grieving' with a single word; the Peshitta employs a periphrastic adverbial clause ܟܕ ܥܝܝܩܐ ܠܗ ('while it was grievous to him'), using the subordinator ܟܕ plus a dative ethical construction characteristic of Syriac. The Vulgate's colon (idx 6) marks the clause boundary corresponding to the Greek high stop after λυπούμενος·.

Greek ἦν...ἔχων ('he was having') is a periphrastic imperfect rendered by Vulgate erat...habens; the Peshitta uses the existential idiom ܐܝܬ ܗܘܐ ܠܗ ('there was to him'), the standard Syriac construction for possession, plus the dative ܠܗ, with γάρ/enim/ܓܝܪ all attesting the causal particle.
κτήματα πολλά / ܢܟܣܐ ܣܓܝܐܐ / multas possessiones — 'many possessions.'
